case_name: Satish Khatik vs Smt. Sanju Khatik
facts_of_case: The husband appealed against the divorce decree passed by the Family Court. The wife was awarded interim maintenance of Rs. 1500/- per month during pendency of the suit. After termination of proceedings, the husband stopped making payments.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking interim maintenance to establish that they are unable to maintain themselves.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel for the respondent/wife submits that respondent/wife has no source of income. She is only dependent on interim maintenance amount.

legal_principles.principle: A party's income and expenses are relevant factors in determining the quantum of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The appellant earns meager amount in his business. His total income is not sufficient to make both ends meet.

outcome.final_order: The court ordered the husband to pay Rs. 7,000 per month as interim maintenance to the wife from the date of filing the appeal without default.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: representing clients in Family Court proceedings
